what_its_for: Lenalidomide is used to treat certain types of blood cancers and blood disorders, including multiple myeloma (a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow), myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS, a condition where bone marrow does not make enough healthy blood cells), and mantle cell lymphoma. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells and helping your immune system fight the disease.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not open, break, or chew the capsule. You may take it with or without food. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. This medicine comes with a special safety program called REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy). You must be enrolled in this program to receive lenalidomide. Your doctor, pharmacist, and you must all follow the program rules, which include regular pregnancy tests for women who could become pregnant.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, weight, and kidney function. Typical doses range from 5 mg to 25 mg taken once daily. You will usually take it for a certain number of days in a treatment cycle (for example, days 1 through 21 of a 28-day cycle), then take a break. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store lenalidomide at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused capsules down the toilet. Return any unused or expired capsules to your pharmacist or a drug take-back program right away, as directed by the REMS program.
what_to_avoid: Do not donate blood while taking lenalidomide or for at least 4 weeks after stopping it. Do not donate sperm while taking this medicine or for at least 4 weeks after stopping. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant must NOT handle or touch the capsules, as this drug can cause severe birth defects or fetal death. Use two forms of effective birth control at the same time for the entire time you are taking lenalidomide and for at least 4 weeks before and after treatment if you are a woman of childbearing age. Men must use a condom during and for at least 4 weeks after treatment if their partner could become pregnant. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it may increase certain side effects. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medications, vitamins, or supplements, including over-the-counter drugs.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a blood clot such as chest pain, shortness of breath, swelling, redness, or pain in your arm or leg; signs of infection such as fever (temperature above 100.4°F or 38°C), chills, or sore throat; unusual bleeding or bruising; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; numbness, tingling, or burning in your hands or feet; severe skin reactions such as blistering or peeling; yellowing of the skin or eyes; extreme tiredness or weakness; or if you think you or your partner may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Lenalidomide may take several weeks to months before you notice the full benefits. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and check-ups. Do not stop taking the medicine on your own even if you feel well, as treatment often needs to continue for it to keep working. Every person responds differently, so be patient and keep all your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Lenalidomide must NEVER be used during pregnancy. It causes severe, life-threatening birth defects. Women who could become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting, during, and after treatment and must use two reliable forms of birth control. Breastfeeding is not recommended while taking this medicine. Kidney problems: The dose may need to be adjusted if you have kidney disease, including if you are on dialysis. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially blood clots and infections. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: The safety and effectiveness of lenalidomide in children under 18 years of age have not been established.
